title: Hospitalisation and associated costs of gastrointestinal bleeding from primary prevention aspirin use in South Australia: a retrospective case series analysis

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>We assessed hospitalisations for gastrointestinal bleeding directly related to primary prevention aspirin in lower risk patients for a 6‐month period in three South Australian hospitals. Those with related underlying pathology or concurrent causative medication were excluded. Identified patients (<jats:italic>n</jats:italic> = 22) carried little co‐morbidity, 41% received prior proton‐pump inhibitors and 68% were aged >70 years. Mean hospital admission cost was $6769 (95% confidence interval $5198–$8340), with projected state and national annual costs of $0.57 and $8.12 million respectively. In light of recent guideline changes, clinicians need to vigorously assess the need for primary prevention aspirin.</jats:p>
